properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued October 4 at 11:01PM PDT until October 7 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Hot conditions with maximum temperatures in the mid-90s to
low-100s. Mild minimum temperatures and weak onshore flow will
limit overnight relief.

* WHERE...The East Bay and San Francisco Bay Shoreline, North Bay
Interior Mountains and Valleys, The Santa Clara Valley and Eastern
Hills, The Santa Cruz Mountains, Interior Monterey County and the
Santa Lucia Range, Most of San Benito County and the Cholame Hills
in Southeast Monterey County, and Southern Salinas Valley/Arroyo
Seco and Lake San Antonio.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...For the Heat Advisory, this level of heat affects anyone
without effective cooling and/or adequate hydration. Impacts likely
in some health systems, heat-sensitive industries and
infrastructure.
properties.instruction:
Hydration is a critical piece to surviving the heat. Drink water, and
if possible, take water to those who are vulnerable.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to the early
morning or evening. Take action when you experience symptoms of heat
exhaustion and/or heat stroke.

Beat the heat and check the backseat! Do not leave young children or
pets in unattended vehicles. Car interiors will reach lethal
temperatures in a matter of minutes.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 5 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
Widespread fog has formed across many of the river and mountain
valleys across the State of West Virginia and far western
Virginia. Some of the fog may be dense, with visibilities falling
to one-quarter mile or less. Fog will last into the morning
commute. Slow down, use low beam headlights, and keep extra
distance between your vehicle and other vehicles. Fog will begin
to dissipate by about 9 AM EDT this morning.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 5 at 1:51AM EDT until October 5 at 4:45AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Coffee County in southeastern Alabama...
Northern Dale County in southeastern Alabama...

* WHEN...Until 345 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1251 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Up to 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 2 inches are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Elba, Fort Rucker, Enterprise, Ozark, New Brockton, Ariton, Lee,
Tabernacle, Eanon, Camp Alaflo Bsa, Mixons Crossroads,
Clintonville, Java, Victoria, Greater Salem Church, Shell Army
Field, Woodland Grove Church, Frisco, Roeton and Rocky Head.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.description:
A Marine Weather Statement has been issued for the following areas...
Coastal Waters from Port Fourchon LA to Lower Atchafalaya River LA
out 20 nm...
Coastal waters from Port Fourchon Louisiana to Lower Atchafalaya
River LA from 20 to 60 NM...
Coastal waters from Southwest Pass of the Mississippi River to
Port Fourchon Louisiana from 20 to 60 NM...
Coastal waters from the Southwest Pass of the Mississippi River to
Port Fourchon Louisiana out 20 NM...

At 1233 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated a cluster of showers, capable
of producing winds to around 30 knots and weak waterspouts. This
cluster of showers is generally located along a line extending from
near Grand Isle to 8 nm west of Louisiana Offshore Oil Port to 24 nm
south of Isle Derniers, moving east at 5 knots.
properties.instruction:
Mariners can expect widespread gusty winds to around 30 knots and
higher waves. Boaters should seek safe harbor immediately until this
activity passes.

Brief, weak waterspouts are possible with this activity. Remain on
alert in case warnings are issued for waterspout development.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or nearest law enforcement
agency. They will relay your report to the National Weather Service
forecast office.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Escambia County in northwestern Florida...
Southern Okaloosa County in northwestern Florida...
Southern Santa Rosa County in northwestern Florida...

* WHEN...Until 300 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas. Some
low-water crossings may become impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1206 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is already occurring in the
advisory area. Between 1 and 3 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Pensacola, Ferry Pass, Brent, West Pensacola, Wright, Fort Walton
Beach, Ensley, Warrington, Niceville, Gonzalez, Destin, Eglin
AFB, Pace, Valparaiso, Gulf Breeze, Goulding, Mary Esther,
Bagdad, Ocean City and Lake Lorraine.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued October 4 at 11:53PM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
At 1152 PM CDT...A line of strong thunderstorms was located along a
line extending from East Santa Rosa Sound to 50 nm southwest of
Oriskany Reef...moving east at 15 knots.

Locations impacted include...
Mary Esther, Navarre Beach, Fort Walton Beach, East Santa Rosa Sound,
Oriskany Reef, Okaloosa Deep Water Reef, Shalimar, Fort Walton
Liberty Ship Reef, Destin, and East Bay.

The primary threats from these storms are wind gusts up to 30
knots...locally higher waves...and heavy downpours. Boaters should
consider seeking safe harbor until these storms have passed.

Weather conditions support the development of waterspouts.
Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally hazardous
waves and seas. If a waterspout is sighted...seek safe harbor
immediately.

These storms may continue to intensify and a warning may soon be
needed. Please continue to monitor local radio or TV for further
National Weather Service updates or possible warnings.

To report severe weather...call (800) 284-9059.

properties.description:
FFWBMX

The National Weather Service in Birmingham has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northern Barbour County in southeastern Alabama...

* Until 230 AM CDT.

* At 1152 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 4 and 6 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Clayton, Comer, Barbour County Public Lake Dam, Spring Hill,
Hawkinsville, Boot Hill, Batesville, Mount Andrew, Clayton
Municipal Airport and Lugo.

This includes US Highway 82 between mile markers 219 and 235.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 4 at 9:48PM PDT until October 9 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor coastal flooding and dangerous rip currents
expected due to the combination of high tides and elevated
surf.

* WHERE...San Diego and Orange County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Moderate flooding of sea water is possibly over
some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas. Moderate beach
erosion is possible to likely.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Elevated surf of 3-6 feet on south and
southwest-beaches. High tides are expected to peak between 6.5
and 7.0 feet during the morning and evenings. There is a
moderate chance that an upgrade to Coastal Flood Advisory
and/or High Surf Advisory will be needed. These products will
likely need to be extended into the weekend.
properties.instruction: Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.
